paragraphs.text: 在侧边栏会话菜单中新增「删除对话」，永久清除该对话的本地记录。
# @ybbmm/dsh-session-delete

**Delete a conversation from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar — recoverably.**
**在 DeepSeek Harness 侧边栏删

versation from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar — recoverably.**
**在 DeepSeek Harness 侧边栏删除对话——而且可以反悔。**

DeepSeek Harness can archive a conversation but never delete one — the session
log accumulates on di

sk forever. This plugin adds the missing action, and does
it the way a desktop product does: into a

recoverable trash, with restore,
with a permanent-delete escalation, and with an audit trail.
> 中文说明 在下方。
## What it adds
| Where | What |
| Session **"…" menu** | A red **Delete conversation** row, after the shipped pin / rename / fork /

archive rows |
| Session **row hover** | A trash button beside the shipped archive and pin buttons |
| **Confirmation dialog** | Names the conversation, states whether the deletion is recoverable, and

— in permanent mode — asks for the title before it unlocks |
| **After deletion** | Reports what ha
ppened, and offers **Restore** and **Delete permanently** on the same dialog |

Deleting the conversation that is currently open reopens a new session in the
same workspace; the di

alog stays open just long enough to acknowledge the
result.
## What exactly is removed
| Artifact | Effect |
| Session log artifact (`~/.dsh/sessions/<project-key>/<session-id>/`, log + lock file) | moved to t

he trash, or removed in permanent mode |
| Projection cache record (`~/.dsh/storages/session_projcac

he/sessions/<id>.json`) | dropped, then re-checked against a late checkpoint write |
| Workspace acc

ounting — membership, saved order, pin, archive mark | released |
| Live session and agent store ent

ries | detached *before* the files are moved, so no writer re-creates the log |
| Attachments (`~/.d

sh/attachments`) | **kept** — content-addressed and shared between sessions |
| Temp spill files | n

ot touched (the host sweeps them by age) |
| Conversations forked *from* this one | **kept**; the di
alog names how many still point at the deleted parent |
## Compatibility

- Built and verified against DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** (Desktop/Web GUI,
Windows, Chinese and

English UI).
- **No runtime dependencies.** The bundle imports only Node built-ins, and
loads nothin

g from `@deepseek-ai/*` at runtime.
- It deliberately builds on a few host internals: the session st

ore and
persistence services, the workspace registry (including `attachSession` and
the pin/archive

sets, which is how a restore puts a conversation back), the
API session controller's list state (for

the `api-session/added` summary),
the storage-domain projection cache, and the API Gateway's runtim

e *SRC*
dispatch for services that carry a `typertRemote` binding plus Remote method
markers. A host

release that reshapes those may need a plugin update — pin
your host version if you depend on this.

Each of those is read defensively:
a missing one degrades the restore to the older files-only behav

iour and is
reported, never thrown.
- The browser half loads the host's UI primitives defensively. I

f a future
host build drops `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, the action still
works with pla
in elements instead of breaking the sidebar.
## How it works

- **Host half** (`index.js`) registers a `sessionDelete` service with a
`typertRemote` binding and a

hand-written Remote method marker, which makes
the endpoints reachable through the Gateway without

generated Typert
artifacts. The artifact is located through the store's own `locate()`,
which names

the session directory for the shipped JSONL backend and is
honoured as-is for other layouts — after

the target has been checked against
the store's root. Deletion captures the workspace accounting int

o the trash
manifest before releasing it; restore replays it through the registry's own
`attachSessi

on` / `insertSessionBefore` / `pinSession` / `archiveSession`,
which is what makes the workspace fol

low stream update the sidebar, and
emits the inverse of the deletion's `api-session/removed` event
(

`api-session/added`, with the host's own session summary) so the catalog row
comes back too.
- **Bro

wser half** (`client.js`) registers into
`sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item`,
`sidebar.workspaces

.session.row.action` and `shell.overlay`, and calls the
endpoints over the shared connection RPC. Th

e dialog is keyed by the
Session it deletes, so one request's in-flight/error/success state never
le

aks into the next. After a restore it asks the session catalog for a
refresh (when that service exis

ts) so a host that could not build a summary
still renders the restored row.
- Styles copy the host'

s own geometry, renamed under a plugin prefix, and use
only `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, so light/d

ark and theme switching follow
the app.
## Known limitations

- **No toast.** The workspace toast slot's key domain is closed to third-party
plugins; the dialog's

in-place acknowledgement is the confirmation instead.
- **UI copy is English and Chinese only.**
-

Deleting a conversation does not delete files the conversation *produced* in
your workspace — only t

he conversation itself.
- A conversation created but never written to disk has no artifact; deleting

it
releases the row and reports `removed: false`, but the empty slot can linger
in the Host's in-me

mory pending list until the next restart.
- The search index (`dsh-session-query-sqlite`) reconciles

against the
persistence listing on every query, so it drops the deleted conversation on
the next se

arch rather than eagerly.
- The trash is a plain directory next to the session store. It is not shar

ed
between machines and does not sync.
- **Restore is only as exact as the host API allows.** The wo

rkspace registry
has `attachSession` (which prepends) and `insertSessionBefore`, not an
"insert afte

r"; the recorded slot is restored when the session that followed
the deleted one still exists, other

wise the conversation is accounted at the
front. Pinning always prepends, so a restored pin is in th

e pinned set but
may not hold its old position among the pinned sessions. The workspace
projection i

tself is followed by the browser's own workspace stream, so no
extra client RPC is needed for it.
-

A restore that could not reattach the workspace accounting leaves the files
and the row metadata in

place and reports `needsRestart: true`; the next
launch re-adopts the session through the host's his

ts `needsRestart: true`; the next
launch re-adopts the session through the host's history bootstrap.
